note: Spector replay: every @typespec/http-specs mock request sent to typespec-hono and to the GraphQL surface with one handler behind both. Floors: entries compared, as a success value, a 404 null and a top-level error. Ceilings: every entry not compared, by why; rest-* are findings, corpus-*, expected-refusal and old-version entries no server should serve as the corpus has them, each listed with its reason. The full list of what was found is in .out-replay/report.json. Held by test/support/ratchet.ts.

loosened.reason: The harness now sends each request as spector's client does (a body's content type wins, its \: unescaped), mounts the routes under the @server path, and hands response headers in their declared types: 18 more entries compared. Entries no server should serve as the corpus has them are counted in classes of their own, each listed with its reason in report.json: expected-refusal (the corpus answers an error and REST refused), old-version (a version older than the one served), corpus-undeclared-route (a next link no operation declares), corpus-request-violates-document and corpus-response-violates-document (judged by the document @typespec/openapi3 publishes, not by either server).
